t: Of the unobligated balances available in the “Nonrecurring Expenses Fund” established in section 223 of division G of Public Law 110–161, $225,000,000, in addition to any funds otherwise made available for such purpose in this or subsequent fiscal years, shall be available for buildings and facilities at the National Institutes of Health.

fable.w: This is a pure appropriations provision that makes unobligated balances from the Nonrecurring Expenses Fund available for NIH buildings and facilities. No tempting opposite reading exists: it involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision.
fable.s: shall be available for buildings and facilities at the National Institutes of Health.

qwen_block.w: This section is a standard appropriations provision that authorizes the use of specific funds for buildings and facilities at the National Institutes of Health. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process with parties outside the federal government. There are no advisory boards, public comment periods, or requirements to consult with states, tribes, or the public mentioned in the text.
qwen_block.s: Of the unobligated balances available in the “Nonrecurring Expenses Fund” established in section 223 of division G of Public Law 110–161, $225,000,000, in addition to any funds otherwise made available for such purpose in this or subsequent fiscal years, shall be available for buildings and facilities at the National Institutes of Health.

opus.w: This section is a pure funding provision. It makes $225,000,000 from the Nonrecurring Expenses Fund available for buildings and facilities at the National Institutes of Health. It involves no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government is involved. Like Example 1, it only says what funds can be used for, so it is not participation.
opus.b:
1. **Thinking it through.** The only possible trap is that the text names an institution (NIH), which might make it look like some process is involved. It isn't. The section only moves $225,000,000 of unused money in the Nonrecurring Expenses Fund to NIH buildings and facilities. It requires no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue, and no one outside the federal government takes part.

qwen_chat.w: This section is an appropriation provision that authorizes the use of specific funds for construction at the National Institutes of Health. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or interaction with parties outside the federal government (such as the public, states, or private entities) before making a decision. The mere allocation of funds for a federal agency's facilities does not constitute participation as defined.
qwen_chat.s: Of the unobligated balances available in the “Nonrecurring Expenses Fund” established in section 223 of division G of Public Law 110–161, $225,000,000, in addition to any funds otherwise made available for such purpose in this or subsequent fiscal years, shall be available for buildings and facilities at the National Institutes of Health.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the funds are for the National Institutes of Health (NIH), which often involves public input or advisory committees, this implies participation. However, the text itself is purely an appropriation clause specifying the amount and purpose of funds. It does not mandate any consultation, hearing, or interaction with outside parties. The definition requires that the section *itself* involve participation (consultation, coordination, etc. with non-federal entities). An appropriation of funds for construction does not inherently require such interaction.
